text:
devon: Heads-up — saw a CPU regression on prod-serving-3 after deploy abc123. p99 token throughput dropped ~18%. I ran a quick perf capture and the flamegraph shows a surprising amount of sampling in Python scheduler paths and gettimeofday.
maria: ugh. can you paste the perf commands and a tiny summary? :eyes:
devon: ran locally on the worker process (pid 12345):
```bash
perf record -F 400 -g --call-graph dwarf -p 12345 -o perf.data -- sleep 60
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
Summary (approx):
- ~22% _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault / Python frame eval
- ~15% std::mutex::lock / lock contention (kvcache read/write)
- ~12% memcpy (tokenizer buffer copies)
- ~8% gettimeofday / time syscall (used for per-request logging/checks)
naj: interesting. two hypotheses:
1) A recent change added per-token timing checks in Python, which calls time.time() each token — that explains the gettimeofday hit and Python overhead.
2) kvcache is using a single global lock for reads; under batching it serializes scheduler threads -> mutex hotspots in C++.
tara: +1 on both. also note perf's sampling bias with Python: the GIL means samples tend to land in the Python interpreter. do an offcpu or use perf record -g -k to capture syscalls? try `perf record -e sched:sched_switch -a` or use `trace-cmd` for off-CPU stalls.
devon: I re-ran with off-cpu analysis and `perf record -e linux:offcpu -g -p 12345` — saw many threads blocked on futex/condvar around kvcache eviction path. so it's both CPU in Python and blocking sync in C++.
maria: steps to reproduce reliably? we need a small trace we can share in the issue.
devon: repro script: spawn N=32 concurrent batch requests with seq_len=1024, batching window=20ms. The regression only shows up when batch sizes > 16 and bursty arrival.
aj: quick mitigation ideas:
- stop calling time.time() on the hot path; replace with a cached thread-local monotonic timestamp updated less frequently.
- shard the kvcache with per-shard locks (e.g., 64 shards) to reduce contention.
- eliminate an extra memcpy in tokenizer by using string_view-like slices or preallocating buffers.
perf-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/perfdata/1798765432/perf.data and flame.svg
tara: for long-term: add perf-based regression test that runs the bursty-repro in CI with perf sampling and checks top-5 symbols for >10% delta. Also add a microbenchmark for kvcache with concurrent readers/writers.
devon: I'll open two PRs: one to remove the per-token timing checks (small Python change) and one to prototype sharded kvcache (C++). I'll attach perf before/after in the PR description.
maria: awesome. please add the reproduction command and the perf record pipeline in the PR so PMs/eng can reproduce.
aj: one more note — when generating flamegraphs for Python-heavy processes, use `perf record -F 400 -g --call-graph dwarf` and then `perf script --no-demangle | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl` to avoid symbol bloat from JITs. also consider `py-spy record -o svg --native` for a Python-aware view.
devon: thanks — assigning action items in the issue now. cc @tara for the regression test.
perf-bot: noted. benchmark job queued: bench/kvcache-shard-proto#257

maria: :thumbsup: keep notes in the perf ticket and paste the flame svg into the PR.
